details:
Standard avatar gesture editor. I think many people are familiar with the "Dynamic Gestures" prefab for avatars, which allows you to swap gestures on the fly by double-tapping the grab button. Usually, this is used to show a middle finger instead of the standard Rock'n'Roll gesture. Personally, I use the "Italian pinch" most of the time. This gave me an idea: since gesture animations rely on a limited set of universal parameters strictly limited to bone rotations, a feature could be added to the menu for editing and selecting custom gestures to replace the standard ones. Currently, the menu only has a basic on and off toggle for gestures. Comprehensive presets could be introduced where users create their own gestures to override the defaults. Since direct access to the IK system and avatar skeletons is available at the platform level, a native interface could be implemented. Created gestures would be saved locally to the user's profile and only a simple gesture ID would be transmitted over the network completely bypassing the standard avatar expression parameter limits.

At first, I thought this feature would lose relevance when the Frame comes out. However, given the expected price, it seems that Valve Knuckles style four-finger tracking will remain a privilege of the minority. Furthermore, it would be a fantastic feature for Oculus standalone Android users to have without needing to upload their own custom avatars.
title: In-game avatar gesture editor
